scenario: WIBTA for testing my boyfriend? | So a short backstory on me, I am a model. And with that most of my previous relationships stem from the guys I am dating on really dating me because of my looks and the "status symbol" of dating a model not because of me as a person. This is something that has caused a lot of anxiety and depression in my life and I have been really trying to find people in my life that care about me not what I look like. Now that is not to say that my looks can't play a role (physical attraction is important to me as well) but I can't be with anyone where that is the only or main reason why they are dating me. So that brings me to a guy a started dating fairly recently. I really like him and he seems like a good guy. Takes interest in my hobbies and is supportive of what I do. He enjoys lazy days around the house and cooking for me at home instead of always wanting to go out (which with a lot of guys it just seemed like they wanted to show me off). So I really really like him. But his friend DM'd me the other day and told me, "Hey, just thought you should know. You boyfriend has been telling anyone who will listen about all the dirty shit he gets to do with 'this model chick I have been banging'. I'd want to know. Hope for the best!" I have only met this guy once and I don't know how close he is to my boyfriend nor do I know why he told me this. For all I know he is just trying to start drama. The problem is I know how badly I want to believe my boyfriend. And if he were to tell me that it isn't true I would probably believe him. But that thought of "what if" would constantly be in my head from now on. So would I be an asshole if for the next month or so I stop wearing makeup when we go out and I don't put out at all (just come up with whatever excuse I need to when he starts trying to make a move)? If I test what his motives truly are? Part of me feels like this is wrong but the other part knows this is the only way I can fully 100% put this behind me. And if his friend is lying I can commit to him 100%

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out what to do in this situation. I'm a model, and most of my past relationships have been with guys who were more interested in my looks and the status of dating a model rather than me as a person. This has caused me a lot of anxiety and depression, and I really want to find someone who cares about me for who I am, not just my looks. That's not to say that physical attraction isn't important to me, but I can't be with someone where that's the only or main reason they're dating me. Now, I'm dating this guy who seems really good. He takes interest in my hobbies, supports what I do, and enjoys lazy days at home, cooking for me instead of always wanting to go out, which a lot of guys seem to do just to show me off. I really like him, but there's this issue that came up recently. His friend DM'd me and told me that my boyfriend has been telling anyone who'll listen about all the "dirty shit" he gets to do with "this model chick I've been banging." The friend said they just thought I should know and hoped for the best. I've only met this guy once, and I don't know how close he is to my boyfriend or why he told me this. For all I know, he's just trying to start drama. The problem is, I really want to believe my boyfriend. If he were to tell me it's not true, I would probably believe him. But the thought of "what if" would constantly be in my head from now on. So, would I be an asshole if, for the next month or so, I stop wearing makeup when we go out and don't put out at all (just come up with whatever excuse I need when he starts trying to make a move)? If I test what his motives truly are? Part of me feels like this is wrong, but the other part knows this is the only way I can fully, 100%, put this behind me. And if his friend is lying, I can commit to him 100%. I'm really torn here. On one hand, I want to trust my boyfriend, but on the other hand, I want to make sure that he's not just interested in me for superficial reasons. I don't want to be hurt again, but I also don't want to ruin a good relationship by being overly suspicious. Maybe I should talk to him about it directly. But what if he gets defensive? Or what if he thinks I don't trust him? I don't want to create unnecessary tension in our relationship. But at the same time, I need to feel secure and confident in our relationship. Perhaps I should also consider the possibility that his friend is lying or exaggerating. Maybe it's just a misunderstanding. But how can I be sure? I guess I could ask my boyfriend about it, but I'm not sure how to bring it up without making him feel accused. Another thought: maybe I should focus on the qualities I like about him and see if those things remain consistent. If he continues to show genuine interest in me as a person, then maybe the rumors aren't true. But if he starts acting differently, that might be a sign. I'm also wondering if there's a way to test his motives without being manipulative. Maybe by observing his behavior over time and seeing if he's more interested in getting to know me or just the physical aspect of the relationship. Overall, I'm feeling a lot of uncertainty and anxiety. I want to make the right decision, but I'm not sure what that is. I need to find a balance between protecting myself and trusting my boyfriend.
